title: heap buffer overflow in ast _copy_characters
live_proof: measured, not asserted: the trigger runs on the pinned 3.13.7 ASan build (PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0) and reports ASAN:heap-buffer-overflow in a 97-byte region. Running it is the liveness proof -- a sanitizer report here means the defect is present in this tree.
fidelity: the trigger is upstream's own reproducer from the issue, run through the real interpreter rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it.
layer_note: measured: ASan reported a 97-byte region, at or under the 512 B SMALL_REQUEST_THRESHOLD

spatial.oracle: no bounds fault is admissible: pymalloc sub-allocates inside an arena, so the stale access stays within the bounds of the capability that covers it. The base arm does enforce revocation (CAPSTONE_REVOCATION_ENFORCE defaults to 1 and is independent of the sublet discipline), so the admissible outcomes are completion, or a revoked-capability fault (cause 24) once pymalloc has returned the block's emptied arena to the system allocator. Which of the two occurs is a property of arena occupancy rather than of the defect, so this arm does not separate these cases. A cause 5 or 7 fault would falsify this.

sublet.oracle: fault at the stale access: this arm issues and revokes pymalloc's own blocks

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: complete: pymalloc links the freed block onto its own pool free list and never returns it to libc, so the platform has no free to revoke

status: three arms measured 2026-10-06: cheri11, spatial-20261006-105111, sublet-20261006-112658
